text: A storage event trigger runs a pipeline in response to a real event on a storage account — a file arriving, or a file being deleted — instead of any wall-clock schedule at all. It's built on Azure Event Grid, and currently supports Data Lake Storage Gen2 and general-purpose v2 storage accounts.
From the pipeline's Trigger menu, select Storage events as the type, choose the storage account and the container to actually watch, and set the matching pattern.

Blob path begins with and blob path ends with are genuinely the only pattern matching a storage event trigger supports — no other wildcards at all. At least one of the two is required. Choose whether it fires on blob created, blob deleted, or both.

The trigger captures the arrived file's location as folderPath and fileName. Map these to real pipeline parameters during setup, and any activity in the pipeline can reference them directly — when a file actually lands, these parameters carry its exact path and name straight into your pipeline.

Worth understanding, not just memorizing: Data Factory never polls the storage account or contacts it directly to detect events. It subscribes to Event Grid instead, which pushes the event the moment storage actually reports it — a genuine push model, not a polling loop. Next: Trigger Dependencies and Chaining — making one trigger genuinely wait on another's success.
